title: Internal-Hom cancellation by an invertible tensor factor
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a monoidal category [def-sfb-monoidal-category] with a symmetric braiding $\sigma_{U,V}:U\otimes V\xrightarrow{\sim}V\otimes U$, natural in both variables and satisfying the hexagon and symmetry identities. Suppose it is closed: for every $X$ there is a functor $[X,-]$ and adjunction bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(Z\otimes X,Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Z,[X,Y])$, natural in $X,Y,Z$. Write $e_{X,Y}:[X,Y]\otimes X\to Y$ for evaluation. Let $J,I\in\mathcal C$ have specified isomorphisms $J\otimes I\cong\mathbf1$ and $I\otimes J\cong\mathbf1$; this is the meaning of an invertible tensor factor here. For all $X,Y$ define two morphisms by transposition:
$$t_{X,Y,J}:[X,Y]\otimes J\longrightarrow[X,Y\otimes J],\qquad s_{X,Y,J}:[X,Y]\longrightarrow[X\otimes J,Y\otimes J],$$
where their uncurrying equations, with associators suppressed, are
$$e_{X,Y\otimes J}\circ(t_{X,Y,J}\otimes1_X)=(e_{X,Y}\otimes1_J)\circ(1_{[X,Y]}\otimes\sigma_{J,X}),$$
$$e_{X\otimes J,Y\otimes J}\circ(s_{X,Y,J}\otimes1_{X\otimes J})=e_{X,Y}\otimes1_J.$$
Both $t_{X,Y,J}$ and $s_{X,Y,J}$ are isomorphisms, natural contravariantly in $X$ and covariantly in $Y$. They are also compatible with isomorphisms of the invertible factor $J$. In particular $c_{X,Y,J}=s_{X,Y,J}^{-1}$ is the canonical cancellation isomorphism $[X\otimes J,Y\otimes J]\xrightarrow{\sim}[X,Y]$, and the displayed equations specify the evaluation normalization of these isomorphisms and their inverses.

proof.text: Write $H=[X,Y]$, and let $a:J\otimes I\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1$ and $b:I\otimes J\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1$ be the specified isomorphisms. Define $T_J(A)=A\otimes J$, $T_I(A)=A\otimes I$, with maps $f\otimes1$. The composites have natural isomorphisms $T_I T_J(A)\xrightarrow{\alpha}A\otimes(J\otimes I)\xrightarrow{1\otimes a}A\otimes\mathbf1\xrightarrow{\rho}A$ and $T_J T_I(A)\xrightarrow{\alpha}A\otimes(I\otimes J)\xrightarrow{1\otimes b}A\otimes\mathbf1\xrightarrow{\rho}A$. Each is natural because associators and unitors are natural and tensor is a bifunctor. No triangle identity relating $a$ to $b$ is asserted or required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-quasi-inverse-hom-bijection] to $F=T_J,G=T_I$ and the natural isomorphisms of step 1. Thus $f\mapsto f\otimes1_J$ is bijective on each Hom set. Also every object $Z$ is isomorphic to $W\otimes J$ with $W=Z\otimes I$: use the second displayed composite of step 1 at $Z$. In all subsequent calculations associators are these specified associators; rearranging parentheses is their naturality and the pentagon and triangle identities, not any assumption on the chosen inverse-factor isomorphisms.

proof.text: For any $A$, write $U_X(h)=e_{X,Y}\circ(h\otimes1_X)$ for the adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(A,[X,Y])\to\operatorname{Hom}(A\otimes X,Y)$. Naturality of the assumed adjunction gives $U_X(h\circ k)=U_X(h)\circ(k\otimes1_X)$ and $U_{X\prime}([f,g]\circ h)=g\circ U_X(h)\circ(1_A\otimes f)$ for $f:X\prime\to X$, $g:Y\to Y\prime$. Here $[f,g]:[X,Y]\to[X\prime,Y\prime]$ denotes the induced internal-Hom map. Define $t$ and $s$ as the unique transposes of the two evaluation composites in the statement. This proves their defining equations and existence without using invertibility.

proof.text: For the second map define rightUncurry(f) as the braiding followed by Mathlib uncurrying. It is a bijection, since both operations are bijections. The evaluation equation gives rightUncurry(f followed by s) = inverse-associator followed by (rightUncurry(f) tensor identity_J), using associator and braiding naturality. Tensoring with J is fully faithful by [lem-sf-quasi-inverse-hom-bijection], implemented by tensorRightEquivalenceOfTensorIso(a,b). Hence postcomposition with s is injective. For surjectivity, a map g into its target gives a map (Z tensor X) tensor J to Y tensor J after rightUncurry and the associator. Take its preimage under that fully faithful functor and then its unique transpose. The evaluation equation proves this transpose maps to g. Apply isIso_of_yoneda_map_bijective and take asIso.

source.place: Tags 0FFM (categories-lemma-invertible), 0GWJ (categories-remark-internal-hom-monoidal); agent argument using the displayed evaluation transposes.

proof.text: For $f:X\prime\to X$ and $g:Y\to Y\prime$, the naturality identities are $t_{X\prime,Y\prime,J}\circ([f,g]\otimes1_J)=[f,g\otimes1_J]\circ t_{X,Y,J}$ and $s_{X\prime,Y\prime,J}\circ[f,g]=[f\otimes1_J,g\otimes1_J]\circ s_{X,Y,J}$. Apply the injective uncurrying bijection to each identity. For the first, both sides become $(g\circ e_{X,Y}\circ(1_H\otimes f))\otimes1_J$ after precomposition by the permutation $(H\otimes J)\otimes X\prime\to(H\otimes X\prime)\otimes J$ given by the associator, the braiding of $J$ past $X\prime$, and the inverse associator. This follows from $\sigma_{J,X}\circ(1_J\otimes f)=(f\otimes1_J)\circ\sigma_{J,X\prime}$. For the second, both sides become $(g\circ e_{X,Y}\circ(1_H\otimes f))\otimes1_J$ on $H\otimes(X\prime\otimes J)$, with the inverse associator understood. This proves the two asserted variable naturalities.

source.place: Tags 0FFM (categories-lemma-invertible), 0GWJ (categories-remark-internal-hom-monoidal); agent argument using the displayed evaluation transposes.

proof.text: Let $u:J\xrightarrow{\sim}J\prime$ be any isomorphism of invertible factors; no compatibility with chosen inverse data is needed because the definitions of $t,s$ do not use that data. The precise factor-compatibility equations are $t_{X,Y,J\prime}\circ(1_H\otimes u)=[1_X,1_Y\otimes u]\circ t_{X,Y,J}$ and $s_{X,Y,J\prime}=[1_X\otimes u^{-1},1_Y\otimes u]\circ s_{X,Y,J}$. After uncurrying, both sides of the first equation equal $(e_{X,Y}\otimes u)\circ(1_H\otimes\sigma_{J,X})$ by naturality of the braiding. For the second, uncurrying its right side gives $(1_Y\otimes u)\circ(e_{X,Y}\otimes1_J)\circ(1_H\otimes1_X\otimes u^{-1})=e_{X,Y}\otimes1_{J\prime}$ since $u\circ u^{-1}=1$. This is the uncurry of its left side. Injectivity of transposition proves both equations.

source.place: Tags 0FFM (categories-lemma-invertible), 0GWJ (categories-remark-internal-hom-monoidal); agent argument using the displayed evaluation transposes.

proof.text: Put $q=t^{-1}$ and $c=s^{-1}$. Compose the first defining evaluation equation on the right with $q\otimes1_X$ to obtain $e_{X,Y\otimes J}=(e_{X,Y}\otimes1_J)\circ(1_H\otimes\sigma_{J,X})\circ(q\otimes1_X)$. Similarly the second gives $e_{X\otimes J,Y\otimes J}=(e_{X,Y}\otimes1_J)\circ(c\otimes1_{X\otimes J})$. These are precisely the inverse evaluation normalizations. Multiplying the naturality and factor-compatibility identities of steps 7–8 by the inverse maps proves the corresponding identities for $q,c$. Thus $c:[X\otimes J,Y\otimes J]\xrightarrow{\sim}[X,Y]$ is the canonical natural cancellation isomorphism.
